transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I'm here because... I just don't want to do anything anymore. The things that usually keep me going, they just don't matter right now. I used to go to salsa nights, church gatherings, I'd even cook for my neighbors. But now... I don't have the energy or the desire for any of it. I'm a carpenter, and I used to love just walking into my shop to smell the wood, you know? But lately, I haven't even wanted to do that. It's like someone just turned off a switch.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about two months now. It really started when my wife's health suddenly declined. Our whole daily routine changed overnight, and... well, that's when this whole shift in my mood and behavior began.
Do you still enjoy things you used to like, or has the pleasure gone away as well?

Yeah, like I mentioned a minute ago... the pleasure is just completely gone. I really have stopped wanting to do any of the things that usually keep me going. Even if I force myself to think about going to a salsa night or cooking for the neighbors, there's just no joy in it anymore. Like I said about the shop, I used to love just being in there, but now... I don't get anything out of it. It all just feels empty.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or ending your life?

Well... yes, I have. I've had thoughts that... maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes I catch myself thinking that my family might actually be better off without me. It... it scares me that I'm thinking that way, to be honest, but the thoughts are there.
Have you noticed any changes in your movement or activity level, such as feeling restless or slowed down?

Yes, I have. Actually, even the guys at the job have noticed it. Sometimes it feels like I'm moving like my boots are full of wet cement... it takes me forever just to bend down and pick up a board. But then other times, it's the opposite. I'll get stuck just pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands together, and not actually doing anything useful. It's just one or the other lately.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?
No, I haven't really noticed any changes in my weight. I mean, my clothes still fit the same as they usually do. So, no, I don't think so.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about anything in particular lately?

Yeah, I have. A lot, actually. I just... I keep replaying every doctor's appointment in my head, and every little change in my wife’s health. I keep telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner. That I should have been able to protect her somehow, and I didn't. It just really weighs on me.
Have you ever felt this way before, with a loss of interest in activities and feelings of worthlessness, at any other point in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I've had times where I felt down or stressed out, sure, but... nothing like this. This is the first time it's been this bad, where I just can't seem to care about anything and feel like I'm completely useless.
Have you experienced any unusual thoughts or heard any voices that others couldn't hear?
No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or had any weird thoughts. Just the guilt and the sadness, really.
Would you say your feelings of sadness and lack of interest in activities are constant throughout the day, or do they vary?
I haven't really noticed it changing, to be honest. I mean... it feels pretty constant. From the minute I wake up until I try to go to sleep, it's just... there. It doesn't really let up at all.
Would you say these feelings of sadness and lack of interest have been interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home?

Yeah, it really has. At work... well, I'm a carpenter, and lately I've had to hand off parts of the jobs I normally supervise myself. I just don't have it in me to do it. And outside of work, I've pretty much pulled away from everyone. I've stopped going to church, I avoid my friends, the neighbors... I just isolate myself. It actually got to the point where my wife and the contact at our parish got really worried about my safety.
Would you say your current condition is severe enough that you're unable to function in daily life most of the time?

Yeah, like I was just saying, it really is. I'm just not functioning most of the time right now. Handing off my normal supervisor duties at work... that's a big deal for me. And completely pulling away from everyone—the church, my friends, the neighbors... it got bad enough that, like I mentioned, my wife and the folks at the parish were actually scared for my safety. So, yeah, I'd say it's definitely severe enough that I'm just not able to do my daily life.
Have you been feeling more slowed down physically or more restless than usual most of the time over the past two months?

Yeah, both, honestly. The guys at the job have actually noticed it. Sometimes I just... I move like my boots are full of wet cement, where it takes me forever just to pick up a board. But other times, I get really restless. I'll get stuck just pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands together, and not actually getting anything useful done.
Would you describe your current depressive episode as mild, moderate, or severe?
I'd say it's severe. Like I said, I'm not functioning at work, I'm completely isolated, and people are worried about my safety. It's definitely severe.
